[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance shows developers how to configure Claude Code — the VS Code extension, the CLI, or project-level settings — to route Anthropic model requests through the **Databricks Unity AI Gateway** pilot environment (`acuity-aigov-stage-ue1`). This is a different integration path than the **AWS Bedrock native provider** that Claude Code uses on a standard Gainwell developer workstation (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` + `AWS_PROFILE=dev-bedrock`, set by the VS Code onboarding script). Unity AI Gateway uses a different endpoint URL, a different token type (Databricks personal access tokens, prefixed `dapi`), and gateway-defined model aliases rather than Bedrock model IDs.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Governed model access** — requests flow through a Databricks-hosted gateway rather than an unmanaged credential
- **Consistent model aliasing** — gateway-defined aliases let the platform control which underlying model version is actually served, without each developer hardcoding a specific model ID
- **Configuration options for every surface** — this guidance covers the VS Code extension, the CLI, and project-level `.claude/settings.json`, so each developer or team can choose whichever surface fits their workflow

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

Developers need a documented, repeatable procedure to point Claude Code — via the VS Code extension, the CLI, or project-level settings — at the Databricks Unity AI Gateway's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, using gateway-defined model aliases instead of AWS Bedrock model IDs, without accidentally committing the Databricks personal access token (`dapi...`) to source control.
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#impact-assessment]

#### Impact Assessment

- Without this guidance, developers cannot reliably test the Unity AI Gateway candidate, may misconfigure model aliases and receive unexpected model behavior, or may paste a live token into a file that is not excluded from version control
- Configuring more than one surface with mismatched model aliases produces inconsistent model behavior depending on which surface is active for a given session

page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#principle-1-keep-the-auth-token-out-of-version-controlled-files]

#### Principle 1: Keep the Auth Token Out of Version-Controlled Files

**Description:** The Databricks personal access token (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, prefixed `dapi`) must never be placed in a file that is tracked by git.
**Rationale:** This token grants access to the Unity AI Gateway under the developer's identity; exposure in source control extends the same risk profile as any other API credential leak.
**Application:** VS Code's **User Settings (JSON)** file lives in the user's editor profile (outside the repository) and is an acceptable place for the raw token value. The project-level `.claude/settings.json` in this repository is version-controlled — do **not** place the token there (see [Pitfall 1](#pitfall-1-storing-the-token-in-a-version-controlled-file)).
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#principle-2-use-gateway-model-aliases-not-bedrock-or-native-anthropic-model-ids]

#### Principle 2: Use Gateway Model Aliases, Not Bedrock or Native Anthropic Model IDs

**Description:** The Unity AI Gateway configuration resolves logical, gateway-defined model aliases to actual served models. These aliases are distinct from both native Anthropic model IDs and the AWS Bedrock model IDs used on the native Bedrock provider path (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`).
**Rationale:** Claude Code's default model environment variables (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`) must be set to the current gateway alias, or the gateway will not resolve the request correctly.
**Application:** Obtain the current alias values from the platform team and use them exactly as provided in whichever surface you configure (VS Code, CLI, or `.claude/settings.json`) — do not substitute a Bedrock model ID or a native Anthropic model name. Because gateway aliases can change over time, treat any alias value as configuration to be verified, not a fixed constant.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#principle-3-environment-variables-are-read-at-process-startup]

#### Principle 3: Environment Variables Are Read at Process Startup

**Description:** Both the VS Code extension and the CLI read their configured environment variables when the process (VS Code or the `claude` CLI) starts.
**Rationale:** Changes made to `settings.json` or a PowerShell session's environment after the process has already launched are invisible to it.
**Application:** Always fully restart VS Code (not just "Reload Window") after editing `claudeCode.environmentVariables`, and set CLI environment variables before launching `claude`.
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#pitfall-1-storing-the-token-in-a-version-controlled-file]

#### Pitfall 1: Storing the Token in a Version-Controlled File

**Description:** Adding `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` to the repository's tracked `.claude/settings.json` instead of VS Code User Settings or a session-scoped/User-scoped environment variable.
**Impact:** The token becomes visible to anyone with read access to the repository and to its full git history, even after later removal.
**Prevention:** Keep the token exclusively in VS Code User Settings ([VS Code Extension Configuration](#vs-code-extension-configuration)) or a CLI environment variable ([CLI Configuration](#cli-configuration-powershell)). Use `.claude/settings.json` only for non-secret defaults such as model aliases ([Project Settings Configuration](#project-settings-configuration-optional)). Per Anthropic's official guidance, never put a gateway credential in a project's tracked `.claude/settings.json` — that file is committed and shared with everyone who clones the repository. `.claude/settings.local.json` is only safe for a manually-created file if you add it to `.gitignore` yourself first; Claude Code only adds it to your global git excludes automatically when Claude Code itself writes a setting there.
**Mitigation:** If a token was committed, treat it as compromised: revoke/rotate it in Databricks immediately and remove it from git history per standard secret-exposure remediation.
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#pitfall-2-powershell-env-variables-only-last-for-the-current-session]

#### Pitfall 2: PowerShell `$env:` Variables Only Last for the Current Session

**Description:** Setting `$env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `$env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, etc. in a PowerShell window only applies to that window.
**Impact:** Closing the terminal or opening a new one means `claude` falls back to its previous configuration.
**Prevention:** For routine use, either re-run the `$env:` commands in each new session, add them to your PowerShell profile (`$PROFILE`), or persist them as User-scoped environment variables using `[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(..., "User")` (see [GUID-TECH-IMPL-006](./GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-azure-devops-mcp-server-local-setup-guidance.md#step-2-set-user-scoped-environment-variables-in-powershell) for the pattern).
**Mitigation:** Re-run the environment variable commands before invoking `claude`.
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#pitfall-3-forgetting-to-restart-vs-code-after-editing-settings]

#### Pitfall 3: Forgetting to Restart VS Code After Editing Settings

**Description:** Editing `claudeCode.environmentVariables` and expecting the change to take effect via "Reload Window" alone.
**Impact:** Claude Code continues to use the previously loaded environment; requests may still go to the old endpoint or model.
**Prevention:** Fully close and reopen VS Code (File → Exit, then relaunch) after saving `settings.json`.
**Mitigation:** Restart VS Code; no other action needed.
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#pitfall-4-inconsistent-model-aliases-across-surfaces]

#### Pitfall 4: Inconsistent Model Aliases Across Surfaces

**Description:** A developer configures more than one surface (VS Code, CLI, `.claude/settings.json`) with model alias values obtained at different times or from different sources, and the values no longer match each other.
**Impact:** The same developer gets different model behavior depending on which surface is active for a given session.
**Prevention:** Confirm the exact, current alias strings with the platform/gateway team before configuring any surface, and re-verify periodically — gateway aliases are platform-managed configuration and can change over time.
**Mitigation:** Update the affected surface(s) to the current confirmed alias.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#pitfall-5-treating-the-pilot-endpoint-as-a-production-standard]

#### Pitfall 5: Treating the Pilot Endpoint as a Production Standard

**Description:** Assuming `acuity-aigov-stage-ue1.cloud.databricks.com` is the permanent, enterprise-approved endpoint for all Claude Code usage.
**Impact:** Workflows built against a staging endpoint may break or require reconfiguration once the AI Gateway technology evaluation concludes and a production endpoint is designated.
**Prevention:** Treat this configuration as a pilot for the Unity AI Gateway evaluation ([EVAL-ai-gateway.md](../../../tech-evals/ai-gateway/EVAL-ai-gateway.md)), and watch for a future enterprise-standard endpoint announcement.
**Mitigation:** Update `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on whichever surface(s) you have configured when a production endpoint is announced.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#pitfall-6-token-silently-auto-revoked-or-auto-scoped]

#### Pitfall 6: Token Silently Auto-Revoked or Auto-Scoped

**Description:** Databricks automatically revokes a personal access token that has not been used for 90 days, and applies **auto-scoping** to new long-lived tokens (30 days or longer): it observes API usage for 30 days and then narrows the token to only the scopes actually used.
**Impact:** A token that worked during initial testing can later fail with an authorization error if the gateway calls Claude Code makes fall outside the auto-inferred scope, or if the token sat unused for 90+ days.
**Prevention:** Set a calendar reminder near the token's lifetime/90-day mark. If you manually scoped the token (see [Obtain a Databricks Personal Access Token](#obtain-a-databricks-personal-access-token)), auto-scoping does not apply and this is less of a concern.
**Mitigation:** Generate a new token following the same steps, and update whichever surface(s) you configured with the new value.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#technical-prerequisites]

#### Technical Prerequisites

- Claude Code VS Code extension and/or the Claude Code CLI installed
- Windows workstation with PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7+
- A Databricks user account with access to the `acuity-aigov-stage-ue1` workspace, requested via ServiceNow and approved by the platform/security team (see [Organizational Prerequisites](#organizational-prerequisites) below and [Request Databricks Workspace Access](#request-databricks-workspace-access)) — you generate your own personal access token from this account; see [Obtain a Databricks Personal Access Token](#obtain-a-databricks-personal-access-token)
- Network access to `*.cloud.databricks.com`
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#transition-prerequisite-workstations-onboarded-via-the-standard-vs-code-setup-script]

#### Transition Prerequisite (Workstations Onboarded via the Standard VS Code Setup Script)

If your workstation was set up using the Gainwell VS Code onboarding script, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` will conflict with Unity AI Gateway configuration on **all three surfaces** and must be removed before you proceed. `AWS_PROFILE` and `AWS_REGION` do not affect gateway routing and should be left in place — removing them from your profile would break unrelated AWS CLI/tooling sessions.

1. **Remove `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` from your PowerShell profile.**  
   Open `$PROFILE.CurrentUserAllHosts` in an editor and delete (or comment out) the `$env:CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` line. Restart PowerShell afterward.

2. **Remove `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` from `~/.claude/settings.json`.**  
   Open `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json` and remove only the `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` entry from the `env` block. Leave all other settings (permissions, `AWS_PROFILE`, `AWS_REGION`, etc.) intact.

   ```jsonc
   // Remove only this entry from the "env" block:
   "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1"
   ```

> **Why both locations?** The onboarding script writes `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` to the PowerShell profile (for new terminal sessions) and to `~/.claude/settings.json` (read at Claude Code process startup). When either is set, Claude Code routes to Bedrock regardless of `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. Both must be cleared for the gateway configuration to take effect.

> **Reversibility:** To return to the Bedrock native path, restore `"CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1"` to the `env` block in `~/.claude/settings.json` and re-add `$env:CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK='1'` to your PowerShell profile (or re-run the onboarding script).

page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#configuration-surfaces]

### Configuration Surfaces

Claude Code has two authentication surfaces — **Option A** (VS Code extension) and **Option B** (CLI) — that are mutually exclusive alternatives: choose the one that matches how you primarily run Claude Code. **Option C** (`.claude/settings.json` model defaults) is an optional overlay for CLI users who want gateway defaults declared once rather than passed on every invocation; it is additive to Option B, not a standalone alternative (it carries no auth token). Configure more than one surface only if you actually use Claude Code through multiple surfaces (e.g., both the VS Code extension and a standalone terminal) and want each to route through the gateway; in that case, keep the model alias values consistent across every surface you configure (see [Pitfall 4](#pitfall-4-inconsistent-model-aliases-across-surfaces)).
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#option-a-claude-code-vs-code-extension]

#### Option A: Claude Code VS Code Extension

**When to use:** You primarily use Claude Code through the VS Code extension.
**Objectives:** Point the VS Code extension at the Unity AI Gateway endpoint and current gateway model aliases.
**Prerequisites:** Databricks token available.
**Key Activities:** See [VS Code Extension Configuration](#vs-code-extension-configuration) in Practical Application.
**Deliverables:** Updated VS Code User Settings (JSON) with `claudeCode.*` keys.
**Success Criteria:** After restarting VS Code, Claude Code sessions in the editor respond using the configured gateway model alias.
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#option-b-claude-code-cli]

#### Option B: Claude Code CLI

**When to use:** You primarily invoke `claude` directly from a terminal, independent of VS Code.
**Objectives:** Point a PowerShell session's `claude` invocation at the same gateway endpoint.
**Prerequisites:** Databricks token available.
**Key Activities:** See [CLI Configuration](#cli-configuration-powershell) in Practical Application.
**Deliverables:** Session (or persisted) environment variables and a working `claude --model ...` invocation.
**Success Criteria:** `claude` starts and responds using the specified gateway model alias without an authentication error.
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#option-c-claudesettingsjson-model-defaults-optional--cli-add-on]

#### Option C: `.claude/settings.json` Model Defaults (Optional — CLI add-on)

**When to use:** You have already configured Option B and want gateway model defaults declared once in the project rather than re-typed or re-exported every session. **Do not use Option C alone** — it contains no `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and will fail authentication without the credentials from Option B.
**Objectives:** Declare non-secret model and endpoint defaults in `.claude/settings.json` so the CLI picks them up automatically.
**Prerequisites:** Option B configured; a confirmed, current model alias from the platform team.
**Key Activities:** See [Project Settings Configuration](#project-settings-configuration-optional) in Practical Application.
**Deliverables:** A `model` and `env` block in `.claude/settings.json` containing no secrets.
**Success Criteria:** `claude` picks up the default model without a `--model` flag, and no token is present in any tracked file.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#practical-application]

## Practical Application

First request workspace access (if you don't already have it) and generate a Databricks personal access token (both below), then read [Configuration Surfaces](#configuration-surfaces) to choose between Option A (VS Code) and Option B (CLI) — they are mutually exclusive authentication paths. Option C (`.claude/settings.json` defaults) is an optional add-on to Option B, not a standalone alternative. All examples use placeholder values in angle brackets (e.g., `<gateway-sonnet-alias>`) — replace these with the current values provided by the platform/gateway team, not with a literal string copied from this document. Each placeholder names a **model tier** (Sonnet, Opus, Haiku); the actual alias value the platform team gives you may or may not contain that tier name as text — use whatever value they provide for that tier, verbatim.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#obtain-a-databricks-personal-access-token]

### Obtain a Databricks Personal Access Token

Databricks personal access tokens (PATs) are workspace-scoped, self-service credentials — any user with workspace access can generate their own. Do this once, in the `acuity-aigov-stage-ue1` workspace:

1. In the `acuity-aigov-stage-ue1` Databricks workspace, click your username in the top bar and select **Settings**
2. Click **Developer**
3. Next to **Access tokens**, click **Manage**
4. Click **Generate new token**
5. Enter a name that helps you identify this token later, e.g. `Claude Code — <your name>`
6. Set the token's lifetime in days — a shorter lifetime (e.g. 90 days) is preferable to a long-lived or non-expiring token
7. Select a scope: choose **Other APIs** and select only the scopes the platform team confirms are required for Unity AI Gateway access, rather than granting all-APIs access. If you are unsure which scope to select, ask the platform team before generating the token — do not default to unscoped/all-APIs access
8. Leave **Auto-scope tokens** off if you scoped the token manually in the previous step; auto-scoping is intended for tokens created without a manually selected scope
9. Click **Generate**
10. **Copy the displayed token immediately** — Databricks shows it only once. It is prefixed `dapi`. Click **Done**

> **Note:** Each Databricks PAT is valid for only the workspace it was created in (`acuity-aigov-stage-ue1` here), so a token from a different Databricks workspace will not work against this gateway. Databricks also recommends OAuth over PATs where available; this guidance uses a PAT because that is what the Unity AI Gateway pilot's `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / bearer-token flow expects today.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#vs-code-extension-configuration]

### VS Code Extension Configuration

Use this surface if you primarily use Claude Code through the VS Code extension.

1. Press **`Ctrl+Shift+P`** to open the Command Palette
2. Search for and select **"Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)"**
3. Add the following block (merging with any existing settings — do not replace the whole file):

   ```jsonc
   {
     "claudeCode.disableLoginPrompt": true,
     "claudeCode.environmentVariables": [
       { "name": "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "value": "https://acuity-aigov-stage-ue1.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/anthropic" },
       { "name": "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "value": "<your-databricks-token>" },
       { "name": "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY", "value": "1" },
       { "name": "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS", "value": "1" },
       { "name": "ANTHROPIC_MODEL", "value": "<gateway-sonnet-alias>" },
       { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL", "value": "<gateway-sonnet-alias>" },
       { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL", "value": "<gateway-opus-alias>" },
       { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL", "value": "<gateway-haiku-alias>" }
     ]
   }
   ```

   `claudeCode.disableLoginPrompt` is the VS Code extension's documented setting for third-party/gateway setups (Settings UI: **Disable Login Prompt**) — it skips the extension's claude.ai sign-in flow so it uses the gateway credential instead. `claudeCode.environmentVariables` is the extension's own credential source: the extension checks it before launching, so the gateway endpoint and token must be set here (not only in `~/.claude/settings.json`) for the login-skip to take effect. Replace `<your-databricks-token>` with your actual `dapi...` token, and each `<gateway-*-alias>` with the current alias provided by the platform team. This file lives in your VS Code user profile (not this repository), so it is not committed to source control — see [Principle 1](#principle-1-keep-the-auth-token-out-of-version-controlled-files).

4. Close the `settings.json` editor tab
5. **Fully restart VS Code** (File → Exit, then relaunch — not just "Reload Window", per [Pitfall 3](#pitfall-3-forgetting-to-restart-vs-code-after-editing-settings))

**Expected result:** After restart, Claude Code sessions in VS Code route through the Unity AI Gateway and respond using the configured gateway model alias by default.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#cli-configuration-powershell]

### CLI Configuration (PowerShell)

Use this surface if you primarily invoke `claude` directly from a terminal, independent of VS Code.

Open PowerShell and set the following session-scoped environment variables, then launch `claude` with an explicit model:

```powershell
$env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "https://acuity-aigov-stage-ue1.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/anthropic"
$env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "<your-databricks-token>"
$env:CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS = "1"
$env:CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY = "1"

claude --model <gateway-sonnet-alias>
```

> **Choosing a tier:** `--model` accepts whichever gateway alias you pass it — substitute `<gateway-opus-alias>` or `<gateway-haiku-alias>` instead of `<gateway-sonnet-alias>` to start the CLI against a different model tier for that invocation.

> **Note:** Confirm the exact model alias with the platform team before relying on it — do not assume it matches an alias you may have configured on another surface without verifying. See [Pitfall 4](#pitfall-4-inconsistent-model-aliases-across-surfaces).

> **Session scope:** These `$env:` values only apply to the current PowerShell window (see [Pitfall 2](#pitfall-2-powershell-env-variables-only-last-for-the-current-session)). To persist them across sessions, either add the same lines to your PowerShell profile (`$PROFILE`) or set them as User-scoped environment variables:
>
> ```powershell
> [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "https://acuity-aigov-stage-ue1.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/anthropic", "User")
> [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "<your-databricks-token>", "User")
> [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS", "1", "User")
> [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY", "1", "User")
> ```

**Expected result:** `claude` starts, authenticates against the Unity AI Gateway, and responds using the specified model alias.

### Project Settings Configuration (Optional)

Use this surface if you use the CLI regularly on a given project and want gateway defaults declared once rather than re-typed or re-exported every session. This is additive to, not a replacement for, Option B — it removes the need to pass `--model` on every invocation.

Declare non-secret defaults in a `.claude/settings.json` (project- or user-level). Unity AI Gateway model entries are referenced by their full Unity Catalog three-level name (`<catalog>.<schema>.<model-alias>`, e.g. `aigov_stg.claude-test.<gateway-haiku-alias>` in the pilot environment) — use the qualified name in `availableModels`, and the bare model alias in the top-level `model` key and the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` variables:

```jsonc
{
  "model": "<gateway-sonnet-alias>",
  "availableModels": [
    "aigov_stg.claude-test.<gateway-haiku-alias>",
    "aigov_stg.claude-test.<gateway-sonnet-alias>",
    "aigov_stg.claude-test.<gateway-opus-alias>"
  ],
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://acuity-aigov-stage-ue1.cloud.databricks.com/ai-gateway/anthropic",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS": "1",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<gateway-sonnet-alias>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<gateway-opus-alias>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<gateway-haiku-alias>"
  }
}
```

The top-level `model` key sets Claude Code's default model and takes precedence over any `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variable, so `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` is omitted here to avoid redundancy. `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` in the `env` block controls per-tier defaults when Claude Code selects a model class automatically. `availableModels` advertises the full set of gateway-qualified model names Claude Code can offer in its model picker; it works alongside `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` rather than replacing it — confirm with the platform team whether your Claude Code version needs this list declared explicitly or discovers it automatically from the gateway.

> **Do not add `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` to this file.** If this is the repository's tracked `.claude/settings.json`, the file is committed to git and any token placed in it becomes part of the repository's history. Keep the token exclusively in VS Code User Settings ([VS Code Extension Configuration](#vs-code-extension-configuration)) or a session/User-scoped environment variable ([CLI Configuration](#cli-configuration-powershell)); use this file only for the non-secret `model`, `availableModels`, and `env` defaults shown above.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#troubleshooting]

#### Troubleshooting

**Authentication error against the gateway:** Confirm the token has not expired, was not auto-revoked after 90 days of inactivity, and was copied without extra whitespace. Also confirm you are using the **token value itself** (the `dapi...` string displayed at creation time) and not the **Token ID** shown in the Databricks Access Tokens dashboard — the Token ID is a numeric or UUID identifier, not a credential, and will fail authentication. Databricks personal access tokens are shown only once at creation — generate a new one following [Obtain a Databricks Personal Access Token](#obtain-a-databricks-personal-access-token) if lost.

**Can't find "Generate new token" or "Manage" in Databricks Settings → Developer:** You likely don't have workspace access yet — submit the [Genius Databricks Access request](#request-databricks-workspace-access) and wait for it to be approved before generating a token.

**Model responses don't match the expected alias:** Check for a mismatch between the alias set on whichever surface(s) you have configured (VS Code, CLI, and/or `.claude/settings.json`) — see [Pitfall 4](#pitfall-4-inconsistent-model-aliases-across-surfaces). Also confirm `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` is set to `"1"` so Claude Code queries the gateway for available models rather than relying on a cached list.

**VS Code Claude Code extension still uses the old configuration:** Fully restart VS Code rather than reloading the window (see [Pitfall 3](#pitfall-3-forgetting-to-restart-vs-code-after-editing-settings)).

#### Organizational Compliance

- Databricks personal access tokens must follow the same credential lifecycle discipline as any other API credential — rotate on or before expiry, revoke immediately if suspected compromise
- Tokens must never be committed to any repository, pasted into chat interfaces, or shared via email or messaging platforms
- Per Anthropic's official Claude Code guidance, a gateway credential must never be placed in a project's tracked `.claude/settings.json`. If your team wants a local, gitignored override file (`.claude/settings.local.json`) for this repository, add it to `.gitignore` before writing a credential there by hand — Claude Code only adds that exclusion automatically when it saves the setting itself

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-012-databricks-unity-ai-gateway-claude-code-setup-guidance.md#risk-assessment]

#### Risk Assessment

| Risk Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Credential exposure | Auth token placed in a version-controlled `.claude/settings.json` | Low | High | Keep tokens exclusively in VS Code User Settings or session/User-scoped environment variables; never in tracked project files |
| Over-scoped token | Token generated with all-APIs access instead of the minimum scopes the gateway needs | Low-Medium | Medium | Select **Other APIs** and choose only the scopes confirmed by the platform team when generating the token (see [Obtain a Databricks Personal Access Token](#obtain-a-databricks-personal-access-token)) |
| Pilot/production drift | Staging endpoint (`acuity-aigov-stage-ue1`) treated as a permanent production standard | Medium | Low-Medium | Track the outcome of [EVAL-ai-gateway.md](../../../tech-evals/ai-gateway/EVAL-ai-gateway.md) and update the endpoint when a production standard is designated |
| Model alias mismatch | Different aliases configured across whichever surfaces (VS Code, CLI, `.claude/settings.json`) a developer has set up | Medium | Low | Confirm the exact alias with the platform team and apply it consistently across every surface configured |
